qValues.intro: A decay can happen only if its Q value is positive. Q comes from the atomic mass excesses Δ: Q<sub>α</sub> = Δ(parent) − Δ(daughter) − Δ(<sup>4</sup>He), Q<sub>β⁻</sub> = Q<sub>EC</sub> = Δ(parent) − Δ(daughter), Q<sub>β⁺</sub> = Q<sub>EC</sub> − 2m<sub>e</sub>c<sup>2</sup> (1.022 MeV), and Q<sub>p</sub> = −S<sub>p</sub>, Q<sub>n</sub> = −S<sub>n</sub>.
qValues.unseenNote: "Allowed, not observed" means the decay is energetically possible but too slow to see: the α particle must tunnel, a β decay may be forbidden by spin, or a faster mode wins.
